nodes.title: 1. Split - how chunks are chosen
widgets_values:
### Cuts the long track into one chunk per run

Each queued item recomputes the same plan and takes its own slice, so chunks tile the
track exactly - no gaps, no overlaps, nothing passed between runs.

Walking forward from 0: ideal cut = position + `target_seconds`; look for a pause
inside `[min_seconds, max_seconds]`; take the nearest one; otherwise use the ideal;
snap to a whole second. So lengths vary - the target is a preference and pauses win
inside the range.

**`cut_mode`** - `pause` (default) ignores `target_seconds` entirely and lets the
speech decide: it takes the furthest pause still within `max_seconds`, merging
segments too short to generate. Boundaries land in silence, chunk lengths follow the
talking. `silence` aims for `target_seconds` and snaps to a nearby pause if one is in
range. `fixed` uses a strict grid, keeping pauses mid-chunk - try it if speech seems
to start early after a pause.

A time cut only happens when no pause is reachable inside `max_seconds`; that is the
model's length ceiling forcing it, not a preference. The console prints how many
pauses were found - zero means every cut fell on the ceiling regardless of mode.

**`skip_existing`** - chunks already on disk are skipped in milliseconds, so resuming
an interrupted render is just queueing from 0 again. The last chunk always re-renders
because it triggers the stitch.

nodes.title: Name run from audio filename (unlink to type your own)
2. Write + Stitch
widgets_values:
### Saves this chunk, assembles the whole render on the last one

**Trims the extra frame.** LTX returns `duration x fps + 1` frames; keeping the spare
one on every chunk accumulates ~2s of progressive audio slip over a long render, so
each chunk is written at exactly `duration x fps`.

**Uses your original audio.** Each chunk's generated audio is a VAE reconstruction of
what went in, so the final mux uses the untouched track - better quality, and sync
exact by construction.

**`session` and `filename`** come from the audio filename via the namer node below, so
`Interview_02.mp3` renders into `.../Interview_02/` and produces `Interview_02.mp4`.
Unlink either to type your own.

**`fps`** must match `fram_rate` inside the generator, or the trim maths is wrong.
Leave both at 24: frame counts must satisfy `frames % 8 == 1`, and at 24fps every
whole-second duration works while 25/30/50 mostly round down.

**`stop_when_done`** clears the pending queue after the final chunk, so a generous
batch count or Run (Instant) ends by itself. Several pods can share one session
folder - a chunk counts as done when its .mp4 exists, written atomically.

nodes.title: Note: Inputs
widgets_values:
## Inputs

- **Load Portrait** - your person, front-facing, face clearly visible. It drives **both** the first and last frame.
- **Load Voiceover** - your speech track, any length. Use **stereo**; mono often gives weak or no lipsync.

Drop files in `ComfyUI/input/`, or upload them through the nodes.

Guide: [Subgraph](https://docs.comfy.org/interface/features/subgraph)

nodes.title: Note: About LTX-2.5
widgets_values:
# LTX-2.5

LTX-2.5 is Lightricks' open video generation model : fast, local-first, and built for production. Run it locally, fine-tune it for your own use case, or integrate it into your pipeline.

**Key highlights:**

- **Pixel Diffusion** : keyframes-first generation that builds every scene on a grid of high-fidelity keyframes for industry-leading pixel quality
- **Diffusion Video Decoder** : sharper faces, legible text, fewer smears in fast motion
- **Native multishot** : one generation yields multiple connected shots holding character, environment, lighting, voice, and style across cuts
- **Custom Gemma 4 12B text encoder** : retains multiple subjects, actions, lighting, detail, and camera direction across complex prompts
- **Dedicated Prompt Enhancer** *(optional)* : a lightweight model that expands short prompts into rich cinematic instructions
- **Auto Duration** : predicts the right clip length from the described action before diffusion begins
- **Better distilled model** : carries far more quality, prompt adherence, and motion into a smaller, faster variant
- Carried over from LTX-2.3: native 4K, synchronized audio-video

Official model & files: https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5
## What this workflow does

This **First & Last Frame** workflow interpolates between two images. Load a first and a last frame, and the model generates the connected shots in between : holding character, environment, lighting, and style across the transition, with synchronized audio.

## Subgraph parameters

The **First & Last Frame to Video (LTX-2.5)** node is a subgraph. Click the **Enter subgraph** button at the bottom of the node to open its internal graph, where you can inspect and fine-tune every step of the pipeline (conditioning, sampler, CFG guider, VAE decode, and more).

| Parameter | What it does |
|---|---|
| first_frame | Starting image of the transition (load your own image in **Load First Frame**) |
| last_frame | Ending image of the transition (load your own image in **Load Last Frame**) |
| prompt | Text prompt describing the motion, scene, lighting, camera, and style |
| prompt_enhance | *(Optional, off by default)* Toggle the built-in Prompt Enhancer, which expands short prompts into rich cinematic instructions. Requires the separate prompt enhancer model (~10 GB) below and adds ~1-2 min of generation time |
| duration | Clip length in seconds (Auto Duration can predict it from the action) |
| width / height | Output resolution in pixels (e.g. 1280×720) |
| seed | Random seed : set a fixed value to reproduce the same result |
| frame_rate | Frames per second |
| unet_name | Main model: LTX-2.5 distilled transformer (ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors) |
| video_vae | Video VAE used for decoding (ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors) |
| audio_vae | Audio VAE that produces synchronized audio (ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors) |
| clip_name | Text encoder: custom Gemma 4 12B with projection (gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors) |
| prompt_enhance_model | Model checkpoint used by the Prompt Enhancer |

## How to use

1. Download the models listed in **Note: Model Links** and place them in ComfyUI's `models/` folder (the prompt enhancer model is optional - skip it unless you enable **prompt_enhance**)
2. Replace the images in **Load First Frame** and **Load Last Frame** with your own start/end frames
3. Write a prompt describing the transition, optionally toggle **prompt_enhance** for short prompts
4. Set **duration** / **width** / **height** / **frame_rate** (defaults work well) and hit **Queue**
5. To dive deeper, click **Enter subgraph** at the bottom of the main node : every internal step (conditioning, sampler, CFG, VAE decode) can be edited there

nodes.title: Why FLF2V for long renders
widgets_values:
### Both ends pinned to the same portrait

The I2V version starts each chunk from the portrait but **ends wherever it ends**, so
every boundary is a jump from that last frame back to the portrait.

FLF2V pins the **first and last** frame. Feed the same portrait to both and chunk N
finishes on the exact frame chunk N+1 starts on - so the joins are continuous **and**
there is no drift, which the I2V chain cannot manage at the same time.

**The trade:** the subject returns to the portrait pose every chunk (~7s). Seamless,
but it can read as a gentle loop. If the shot is a presenter talking to camera that is
usually what they would be doing anyway; for big gestures it may look repetitive.

**Also:** FLF2V is single-stage - no spatial upscaler pass - so chunks render faster
than the I2V graph but skip that refinement. Worth comparing both on the same audio
before committing an hour-long render to either.

There is no Start Frame node here and no `reanchor_every`: nothing chains, so nothing
can drift. Chunks are fully independent and can be rendered in any order, on any
number of GPUs.
